text:
In April this year my Children and I visited Kakadu with Russell Willis of Willis's walkabout tours to go hiking through Mt Brockman for a week.

Having visited Kakadu i thought I had some idea of what to expect but this trip exceeded all my expectations.

Kakadu was so green after a late wet season with water flowing everywhere but it was so hot n humid and I live in Far North Quensland.

You do not need a guide to do overnight or off track hiking in kakadu but you do need a permit.

Kakadu only allocates 2000 hiking permits a year and the process is difficult because you need to provide them with a map showing your route. If course if you have never been you do not know the route and it is very difficult to obtain this information.

Russell Willis is a bit of a legend at 80 years old he has been hiking in the area and running his tours for about 40 years. 

The area we hiked followed a creek all the way through the massif and showed us a part of Kakadu rarely seen, the silence and the solitude was amazing you could really feel what it may be like to live here before white settlement.

If course like many parts of Kakadu there are rock art sites, in fact some of the most extraordinary in Kakadu or the world. However, part of the permit agreement does not allow for people to share images of the rock art or their locations with others. I guess this is to protect them, as there are no fences or really any protection other than trusting people will do the right thing...but given it took 3 days to reach the art sites it wpuld be a big effort for the casual observer.

At 49 and a bit out of shape I found the hike a bit difficult but so worthwhile and really a dream come true to see the particular painting I was in search of.

It was a small group of only 8 carrying all our.own gear and food etc..for 7 days staying the last night at Cooinda.

On a side note Cooinda serves absolutely great meals with awesome staff.

I feel like I had an authentic experience in Kakadu and one many people will never have the opportunity to experience.

Nathan

The Larrimah museum in contrast, is much more informative and it is free.
